papers.title: Altered heart-brain coupling in awake patients with isolated REM sleep behaviour disorder.
papers.abstract: Isolated REM sleep behaviour disorder (iRBD) represents a prodromal stage of alpha-synucleinopathies, frequently preceding Parkinson's disease and dementia with Lewy bodies. Beyond the characteristic sleep disturbances, alterations in brain-body coupling, reflecting neural peripheral physiological interactions, have yet to be determined. Using whole-night polysomnography, we quantified brain-body coupling via heartbeat evoked potentials (HEPs) across wakefulness, NREM, and REM sleep. Individuals with iRBD (n = 13) were compared with healthy controls (n = 23), alongside analyses of ECG-derived features. During wakefulness, iRBD patients showed altered HEPs over frontal regions between 305 and 445 ms after the R-peak. No significant group differences were observed during NREM or REM sleep, and HEP amplitude alterations were not explained by ECG differences. These diurnal HEP changes may represent a novel quantitative biomarker for iRBD during wakefulness and, in the future, could serve as a marker for phenoconversion to alpha-synucleinopathy.

papers.title: Digitizing episodic memory assessments in Parkinson's disease via natural language processing.
papers.abstract: Parkinson's disease (PD) disrupts episodic memory, undermining patients' well-being. Yet, standard assessments consist in counts of recalled information units, limiting informativeness and scalability. To refine testing, we recruited 74 participants (35 PD patients, 39 controls) who retold an action and a non-action story. We analyzed their verbosity (total and content word production), semantic acuity (conceptual similarity to the stories), and organizational similarity (structural similarity to the stories) using part-of-speech tagging, the cosine similarity of text embeddings, and speech graphs. People with PD were less verbose only when retelling the action story, and they exhibited lower semantic acuity and organizational similarity across stories. Our approach (i) achieved robust discrimination between patients and controls (ROC-AUC = 0.79), mostly driven by action-related metrics; (ii) outperformed traditional cognitive, executive, and episodic memory tests scores (ROC-AUC = 0.70); and (iii) distinguished between PD-MCI and PD-nMCI. Episodic anomalies thus manifest across multiple dimensions that elude standard instruments but can be tapped digitally to enhance cognitive assessments in PD.

papers.title: Echinacoside Attenuates α-synuclein Pathology and Lysosomal Dysfunction in PFF-Induced Models Relevant to Parkinson's Disease.
papers.abstract: Abnormal aggregation of α-synuclein (α-syn) and impaired lysosomal degradation are core pathological features of Parkinson's disease (PD). Echinacoside (ECH), the major active component of Cistanche, has been shown to protect dopaminergic neurons in MPTP-induced PD models, but its effects on α-syn clearance and lysosomal function remain unclear. Here, we established a PD-relevant α-syn pathology mouse model by stereotaxic injection of α-syn pre-formed fibrils (PFFs) into the left striatum of C57BL/6 J mice. Mice were divided into four groups: Control, PFFs, PFFs + ECH20 (low-dose), and PFFs + ECH40 (high-dose). The Control group received intrastriatal injection of 0.9% saline, whereas the other groups received α-syn PFFs. ECH was administered orally at 20 or 40 mg/kg for 1 month after modeling, while the Control and PFFs groups received equal volumes of 0.9% saline by oral gavage. Motor function was assessed by rotarod and pole tests at 1, 3, and 6 months, while tyrosine hydroxylase (TH), phosphorylated α-syn (p-α-syn), and lysosome-related proteins were detected in the substantia nigra. In vitro, SH-SY5Y cells were pretreated with ECH before PFFs exposure to evaluate lysosomal morphology, acidification, and proteolytic activity. BafA1, an inhibitor of vacuolar H+-ATPase, was further used to interfere with lysosomal acidification and lysosomal degradation. Six months after PFF injection, mice exhibited significant motor deficits, decreased TH expression, and increased p-α-syn accumulation, accompanied by abnormal lysosomal aggregation, reduced expression of lysosomal proteins (GBA1, CTSD, CTSB, LAMP2, TMEM175). Oral ECH treatment, particularly at 40 mg/kg, improved motor performance, increased TH expression, reduced p-α-syn accumulation, and partially attenuated lysosome abnormalities. papers.title: AI-guided prioritization of potential FAM171A2 ligands through pharmacophore-aware and receptor-based screening.
papers.abstract: FAM171A2 has recently emerged as a potential therapeutic target in Parkinson's disease because it selectively recognizes α-synuclein fibrils and promotes their neuronal uptake. However, ligand prioritization for this receptor remains challenging because of scarce known binders, the absence of an experimentally resolved ligand-bound structure and the requirement for blood-brain barrier permeability. Here, we established an AI-guided computational screening framework that integrates pharmacophore-aware retrieval, hierarchical receptor-based screening, blood-brain barrier permeability prediction and molecular dynamics-based assessment to prioritize potential FAM171A2 ligands. Starting from 1.41 million compounds, the workflow progressively narrowed the search space to two structurally representative candidates, E634-1386 and F707-2364. papers.title: The effects of dual task training to improve self-efficacy, functional performance, and quality of life in individuals with Parkinson's disease: A study protocol.
papers.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Dual tasking is impaired in Parkinson's disease (PD) and adversely impacts activities of daily living and quality of life. The benefits of different dual-task training modalities and the prioritization strategy (directing attention to both tasks versus shifting between them) in individuals with or without cognitive impairment are unclear. It is also unknown whether motor-cognitive benefits from dual-task training are associated with reduced attentional demand. In addition, lower perceived ability to succeed at a specific task (self-efficacy) is associated with worse motor and non-motor symptoms and quality of life. Higher dual-task performance may be associated with higher self-efficacy, which in turn improves dual-task performance. This protocol describes a study evaluating the effectiveness of different dual-task training modalities (motor-motor vs. motor-cognitive) and attentional prioritization strategies (fixed vs. variable) on self-efficacy, functional performance, and quality of life in people with PD, with and without cognitive impairments. METHODOLOGY: Using a factorial design nested within cognitive status, participants will be randomized into one of four groups combining task type (motor-cognitive or motor-motor) with priority instruction (fixed or variable). An interdisciplinary team will design individualized programs. In fixed-priority training, attention is maintained on both tasks, in variable-priority training, attention alternates, focusing on the motor task for half the session and on the secondary task for the remainder. All participants will complete 24 individual sessions (3x/week for 8 weeks, 60 minutes each). Outcomes include self-efficacy, motor and cognitive performance, quality of life, and prefrontal cortex activity. EXPECTED RESULTS: This protocol will introduce a person-centered approach to dual-task training, comparing modalities and attentional strategies tailored to cognitive status. AS-ULDAR: a ROS 2-based collaborative robotic platform for upper-limb rehabilitation - systems integration and pilot usability evaluation in a clinical environment.
papers.abstract: Robotic rehabilitation can increase the intensity and personalization of upper-limb therapy, but its clinical translation is hindered by the difficulty of integrating individually validated technical components into a single clinician-ready platform. This paper presents a platform which is intended to be an Auto-calibrating System for Upper Limb Disability Assessment and Rehabilitation (AS-ULDAR), a ROS 2-based platform built around a Franka Emika Panda robot that unifies motor/cognitive assessment, sensorless force estimation, and Cartesian and Human Joint-based Trajectory Tracking within a clinician-oriented GUI. While these functionalities were individually validated in prior work, the present contribution lies in their systems-level integration and in identifying the operational barriers that emerge when deploying such a platform in a real clinical workflow, targeting adult patients with chronic neurological conditions (stroke, Parkinson's, ALS, MCI) and mild-to-moderate upper-limb impairment. The platform was evaluated through a formative usability study: the standalone GUI by five naïve users, and the complete system by seven physiotherapists performing the full clinical workflow (no patients were involved; clinical efficacy is outside this scope). papers.title: Usability and User Satisfaction With a Prototype Weighted Glove in People With Parkinson's Disease: An Exploratory Secondary Analysis.
papers.abstract: Background Upper-limb impairments in Parkinson's disease (PD) can affect reaching, grasping, object manipulation, and other activities required for functional independence. Wearable and glove-based rehabilitation devices may provide opportunities for upper-limb training; however, their clinical potential should be considered alongside the user's experience. This study evaluated user-reported usability and satisfaction with a prototype weighted glove following two weeks of structured upper-limb rehabilitation in people with PD. Methods This exploratory secondary analysis used previously unpublished post-intervention usability data from a previously conducted single-group pretest-posttest quasi-experimental study. Fifteen people with PD who completed a two-week structured upper-limb rehabilitation programme while using the prototype weighted glove were included. Glove loading ranged from 600 to 700 g and was selected according to individual comfort, physical capacity, movement quality, and verbal feedback. The glove was worn throughout supervised rehabilitation sessions conducted six days per week for 45-60 minutes per session. Following the intervention, perceptions were assessed using the Assistive Technology Usability Questionnaire for People With Neurological Diseases (NATU Quest). Quantitative responses were summarized descriptively, and open-ended responses were reviewed descriptively for recurring areas of feedback. Results The mean age was 67.07 ± 7.70 years; 10 participants (66.7%) were male, and five (33.3%) were female. The mean overall NATU Quest score was 4.28 ± 0.32 out of 5. The highest-rated items were ease of learning (4.73 ± 0.46), perceived safety and security (4.67 ± 0.49), and overall satisfaction (4.60 ± 0.51). Physical comfort/fatigue received the lowest score (3.33 ± 0.72). papers.title: Pallidal deep brain stimulation for Parkinson's disease: indications for target selection and perceived outcomes at two centers.
papers.abstract: We retrospectively reviewed Parkinson's disease patients undergoing GPi-DBS at two academic centers to characterize clinical rationale for target selection. GPi was most commonly selected for dyskinesia, followed by dystonia and neuropsychiatric considerations, with clinicians reporting sustained subjective improvement in hyperkinetic symptoms at one year.

papers.title: Brain-computer interfaces for neurodegenerative diseases: A comprehensive review of closed-loop systems from diagnosis to neural rehabilitation.
papers.abstract: Brain-computer interface (BCI) technology serves as an important bridge between the nervous system and external devices and has shown considerable promise for the diagnosis and treatment of neurodegenerative diseases, whose global burden continues to increase: in 2021, more than 57 million people were living with dementia worldwide, with Alzheimer's disease (AD) accounting for approximately 60-70% of cases, while an estimated 11.77 million people were living with Parkinson's disease (PD) in 2021, according to the Global Burden of Disease Study 2021. This growing disease burden, together with the progressive loss of cognitive, motor, and communicative functions, highlights the need for more precise approaches to early detection, functional assistance, and individualized intervention. Conventional diagnostic and therapeutic approaches remain poorly suited to early detection and timely intervention. This paper analyzes the development of BCI technology, from the first detection of electroencephalogram (EEG) signals to the parallel development of invasive and non-invasive systems, and outlines the basic principles of signal acquisition, processing, and decoding, together with the relative advantages and limitations of different approaches. It then focuses on the use of BCI in Alzheimer's disease (AD), Parkinson's disease (PD), and amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS), covering early diagnosis, functional reconstruction, and neuromodulation. The article also discusses the difficulties encountered by BCI technology in terms of technological realization, clinical translation, and ethical considerations, as well as several future research directions, including multimodal fusion, adaptive algorithms, closed-loop control systems, and personalized treatment so as to drive the applications of BCI in precision medicine and in neurological diseases.

papers.title: Acute Effects of Subthalamic Deep Brain Stimulation Withdrawal on Response and Movement Speed in Parkinson Disease.
papers.journal: Neuromodulation : journal of the International Neuromodulation Society
papers.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Previous studies on deep brain stimulation (DBS) effects on cognition in Parkinson disease (PD) mainly investigated single neuropsychologic domains in isolation and have shown mixed results when comparing performance with stimulation switched on (StimON) and off (StimOFF). We examined short-term effects of subthalamic nucleus (STN)-DBS withdrawal across a comprehensive, standardized neuropsychological battery to characterize which cognitive domains are acutely modulated by stimulation. MATERIALS AND METHODS: In this subanalysis of a prospective cohort study (NCT03982953), 16 patients with PD (five female; age 59.6 ± 10.5 years; disease duration 10.3 ± 5.6 years) completed a tablet-based neuropsychologic battery spanning attention, motor speed, learning, memory, executive function, and social cognition, first during StimON and then, after a 30-minute washout, during StimOFF, with dopaminergic medication kept stable. Twenty one paired comparisons were analyzed with Wilcoxon signed-rank tests (Bonferroni-corrected significance threshold p < 0.0024). RESULTS: StimOFF was associated with significantly slower movement time (p < 0.001) in the simplest reaction-time condition, whereas changes in reaction time with more stimuli (p = 0.004) and multitasking speed (p = 0.031) did not survive correction. Measures of inhibitory control, learning, memory, and social cognition were unchanged in this study. CONCLUSION: STN-DBS withdrawal slowed reaction time, while broader cognitive domains remained stable, suggesting a predominant effect on attentional and psychomotor speed rather than a broad, domain-general cognitive effect. Given the modest sample size and short washout period, these findings should be regarded as preliminary and warrant confirmation in larger studies with longer washout intervals.

papers.title: Clinical Determinants of Specialist-Optimized Parkinson's Disease Pharmacotherapy.
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Pharmacological management of Parkinson's disease (PD) is guided by several variables which significantly influence treatment decisions and therapeutic outcomes. This study aims to determine prescription patterns and clinical determinants for optimizing drug treatment of PD in a resource-limited setting by movement disorder specialists at a tertiary care center. METHODOLOGY: In this prospective single-center study, demographic, clinical, and treatment details were recorded at the time of recruitment. The cohort was subclassified for evaluation of the treatment profile based on age at onset (AAO), early-onset PD (EOPD) and late-onset PD (LOPD); motor subtype, tremor-dominant PD (TDPD); postural instability and gait dysfunction (PIGD); indeterminate, age at evaluation; and disease duration. RESULTS: A total of 379 patients were recruited at a mean age of 54.17 ± 11.18 years and 6.14 ± 4.21 years of illness. Levodopa-carbidopa was universally prescribed (>92%). EOPD was more likely to receive dopamine agonists (DAs) (68.78% vs. 42.53%, P < 0.001), amantadine (28.29% vs. 17.24%, P = 0.014), and trihexyphenidyl (30.73% vs. 10.92%, P < 0.001) than LOPD. The PIGD subtype had a significantly higher usage of controlled-release levodopa-carbidopa DA, and amantadine compared TDPD. Younger patients received more DA and trihexyphenidyl; treatment complexity increased with disease duration, particularly with DA and amantadine. CONCLUSION: In conclusion, optimization of prescription patterns in PD is influenced by age, AAO, and motor phenotype. Levodopa-carbidopa is the mainstay of therapy, with younger patients more often receiving adjuncts such as dopamine agonists or amantadine, while older or advanced cases rely mainly on levodopa-based regimens. These findings underscore the need for individualized, phenotype-specific treatment strategies in PD management.

papers.title: Multi-omics profiling suggests deep brain stimulation-associated expansion of CLIC3+ NK cells attenuates neuroinflammation in Parkinson's disease.
papers.abstract: Deep brain stimulation (DBS) alleviates Parkinson's disease (PD) symptoms, but its immunomodulatory mechanisms remain elusive. Through integrating microarray (GSE23676), single cell/nucleus RNA-seq (GSE184950, GSE202210, GSE223138, GSE243639; after quality control (mitochondrial gene content <25%, gene number >200) 616,076 high-quality cells were included), and GWAS data, we identified CLIC3 as a DBS-associated, potential protective implications in PD. CLIC3 was selectively up-regulated in a distinct natural killer cell subset (NK_CLIC3), which secreted TGFB1 to restrain neuroinflammation. CellChat and immunohistochemistry revealed that NK_CLIC3 cells communicated with PD-relevant neuronal populations: excitatory (SLC18A2+), inhibitory (SLC18A2+), oligodendrocyte (SLC18A2+), and astrocytic (SLC18A2+) cells via THY1-ADGRE5 and GZMA-PARD3 axes. Immune infiltration analysis (GSE114517; n = 75) suggested NK infiltration and deficient M2 macrophage recruitment in PD brains, underscoring an inadequate anti-inflammatory response. We further isolated CLIC3-positive NK cells (from a healthy donor) by fluorescence-activated cell sorting (FACS) and confirmed their ability to degrade α-synuclein, the pathological protein in Parkinson's disease, supporting the potential NK(CLIC3+) cells' protective function in PD. Our findings suggest DBS may expand NK_CLIC3 cells to suppress neuroinflammation through TGFB1 mediated immune-neuronal crosstalk, positioning CLIC3 as a prospective therapeutic target for PD.

papers.title: Lactiplantibacillus plantarum alleviates Parkinson's disease progression by reducing enteroendocrine α-synuclein aggregation in a rotenone-induced mouse model.
papers.abstract: Parkinson's disease (PD) is a progressive neurodegenerative disorder driven by α-synuclein (α-syn) aggregation and accumulation. Recent evidence suggests that gut dysbiosis may trigger α-syn accumulation in the enteric nervous system, which spreads to the brain via the vagus nerve. Restoring the gut microbial balance through probiotic intervention offers a promising strategy to mitigate gut-origin pathology in PD. Lactiplantibacillus plantarum PS128 (PS128), a probiotic strain with neuroprotective properties, has shown neurotherapeutic benefits in PD models and patients; however, its mechanisms remain unclear. In a rotenone-induced PD mouse model, we found that PS128 supplementation significantly improved motor deficits and gastrointestinal dysfunction, reversed enteroendocrine cell (EEC) hyperplasia in the proximal colon (PC), and reduced α-syn accumulation in both intestinal and brain tissues. Notably, phosphorylated α-syn levels were significantly elevated in EECs, the myenteric plexus, and the substantia nigra, and these elevations were reversed by PS128. Furthermore, using real-time calcium imaging in a zebrafish model, we demonstrated that PS128 directly activates EECs. Transcriptomic profiling of the PC revealed calcium signaling and vitamin D metabolism as the major pathways modulated by PS128. Consistent with the transcriptomic findings, biochemical analyses demonstrated that PS128 increased serum calcium and 25-hydroxyvitamin D levels. Moreover, 16S rRNA sequencing and correlation analysis revealed that PS128 modulated gut microbiota composition in PD-like mice, with changes in specific taxa correlating with α-syn burden and calcium regulation. Taken together, our findings suggest that PS128 alleviates PD-like pathology through modulation of the gut-brain axis and provide mechanistic insights into the neuroprotective actions of probiotics.

papers.title: Efficacy and safety of non-pharmacological interventions for fatigue in Parkinson's disease: protocol for a systematic review and network meta-analysis.
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Fatigue is a prevalent and disabling non-motor symptom in Parkinson's disease (PD), significantly impairing patients' quality of life. Non-invasive, non-pharmacological interventions, including acupuncture, Tai Chi, and transcranial magnetic stimulation, have gained attention for their favorable safety profiles and cost-effectiveness. However, current evidence is limited by significant heterogeneity in intervention protocols, diverse fatigue measurement scales, and varying methodological quality of existing trials. This study aims to rigorously evaluate the efficacy and safety of non-pharmacological interventions for PD fatigue through a systematic review and network meta-analysis (NMA), providing an evidence-based foundation for clinical practice. METHODS: A comprehensive systematic search will be conducted across eight electronic databases (PubMed, Web of Science, Cochrane Library, Embase, SinoMed, VIP, CNKI, and WanFang) and two clinical trial registries (ClinicalTrials.gov and ChiCTR) from inception to April 20, 2026. Eligible randomized controlled trials (RCTs) comparing non-invasive, single-modality non-pharmacological interventions against inactive controls or active pharmacotherapy will be included. To ensure transitivity and clinical interpretability, the primary outcome will be strictly restricted to the change in Fatigue Severity Scale (FSS) scores, utilizing mean differences. Secondary outcomes will include other fatigue scales, motor symptoms, and quality of life, and systematically categorized adverse events (serious vs. non-serious). Risk of bias will be assessed using the Cochrane ROB2 tool. Pairwise meta-analysis will be conducted using RevMan v5.4 software, and STATA 18.0 will be utilized for NMA, with intervention rankings generated only for nodes meeting a predefined threshold of at least three studies. papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Circulating levodopa and metabolite changes during transition to continuous subcutaneous foslevodopa/foscarbidopa infusion (CSCI), and their relationships with clinical outcomes, remain incompletely characterized. papers.title: Multimodal single-cell epigenomic and 3D genome atlas of the human basal ganglia.
papers.abstract: The basal ganglia (BG) underlie motor control, reward processing, and many neurological and psychiatric disorders, yet cell-type-resolved epigenomic and 3D genome maps of the human BG remain limited. Here, we present a multimodal single-cell atlas of DNA methylation (261,331 nuclei) and 3D chromatin conformation (229,286 nuclei) from eight subregions, harmonized under the BG consensus taxonomy and integrated with matched data across multiple regulatory layers.
